cars.specification_market: US 1969 production-road Spoiler II reference. The surviving Safety & Services Department memo and owner-supplement spread establish the 351 engine and special body parts; the December 30, 1968 release describes the broader Cyclone Spoiler launch and is not proof that all of its gearbox choices reached Spoiler II production. No gearbox, axle, power, torque, production count, measured aero gain, race-engine specification or lower road ride height is inferred. Paint versions and normal-nose Spoilers add no counts.
cars.summary: The Cyclone Spoiler II was Mercury’s road-going aero-homologation counterpart to the Torino Talladega, with dedicated front bodywork and parts rather than only driver-themed paint. Its role in the NASCAR aero era and distinctive production-road engineering justify one original Cyclone fastback family entry. Shared Ford components are acknowledged; the Mercury body/model programme is distinct. Gurney and Yarborough colours, normal-nose Spoilers and engine choices do not add separate counts.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The Cyclone Spoiler II was Mercury’s road-going aero-homologation counterpart to the Torino Talladega, with dedicated front bodywork and parts rather than only driver-themed paint. Its role in the NASCAR aero era and distinctive production-road engineering justify one original Cyclone fastback family entry. Shared Ford components are acknowledged; the Mercury body/model programme is distinct. Gurney and Yarborough colours, normal-nose Spoilers and engine choices do not add separate counts.

media.caption: 1969 Mercury Cyclone Spoiler II in Dan Gurney trim photographed by Carl Sharp. The long smooth nose and fastback body represent the selected road aero family; colour, decals and an exterior view do not certify chassis provenance, engine internals or original equipment. Gurney and Yarborough trim do not create separate entries.
media.creator: Carl Sharp

cars.variant: SST 343 four-speed, 3.54 limited-slip axle — December 1967 road-test reference
cars.specification_market: US model-year 1968 Javelin SST, as tested in Car Life December 1967, printed pages 34–38. This is the 343 V8 four-speed road car, not a 390, shortened two-seat AMX, later Javelin AMX or Trans-Am racer. Go-package content was only partly installed, and the article says stripes were not yet applied; fitted discs/manual steering/limited-slip are not universal standard equipment. Tyre grip and heavy steering limited the test car. No measured performance, weight, production count, full Go-package assertion or modern net/gross label is imported. Other first-generation engines, trim and revisions add no counts. The test table lists five passengers; no four-seat claim from the Commons description is imported.
cars.summary: The original Javelin brought American Motors into the pony-car contest with a distinctive fastback body with rear seating and a serious V8 performance package. The contemporary SST 343 test documents its strong engine, four-speed, limited-slip axle and optional front discs, alongside traction and heavy-steering shortcomings. That landmark AMC sports-coupe programme merits one first-generation road-family entry, separate from the shortened two-seat AMX and later 1971 Javelin AMX. Extra engines, facelifts and appearance packages do not add counts.
